abstract: The development of the lateral olfactory tract (LOT) begins embryonically and is closely linked to the differentiation of olfactory bulb (OB) projection neurons, mitral and tufted cells, whose axons form the LOT. Here, we implemented calretinin (CR) as a proxy to characterize LOT development. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) for CR revealed expression in most mitral/tufted cells, with lower levels in the dorsal OB. This mirrored a reduced CR labeling in a restricted ventral LOT domain, suggesting topographic organization of OB projections. To achieve axonal resolution, we used Calb2-CreERT2 x Ai14 mice to label CR+ neurons and their axons with tdTomato. Expression began at E12, when pioneer LOT axons reach the anterior piriform cortex (APC) and posterior brain regions. From E13-E14, axon density increased, contributing to LOT thickening and extension toward the amygdala. Axonal arborization was not evident in the posterior piriform cortex (PPC) until E15. Electron microscopy revealed excitatory asymmetric and inhibitory symmetric synapses in the APC as early as E13, with relatively stable embryonic densities. Postnatally, excitatory synapses increased in both APC and PPC between P9 and P21. Collectively, this work establishes a developmental timeline of LOT formation and sheds light on fundamental aspects of the assembly of olfactory cortical circuits.
